narrative: Inventory optimization analysis for material PL1__MB5A55F8 reveals a smooth demand regime with CV of 16.87%. The mean daily demand is 113,858 units with unstable lead time variability (CV=55.26%). The optimized policy recommends a safety stock of 154,568 units (vs. SAP's 175,449) and order quantity of 1,433,992 units, resulting in a reorder point of 319,397 units. This policy achieves 95.0% service level with total annual cost of $3,298.42, representing savings of $7,348.04 (69.0%) compared to the previous SAP policy. The recommended safety lead time is 1.36 days versus SAP's 4 days. The dominant variance component is transport at 50%. Capacity utilization is 72.3% of the maximum 2,196,381 storage units.
warnings: Unstable lead times (CV=55.26%) - supplier reliability concern
Recommended SLT (1.36 days) is below SAP SLT (4 days)

research_insights.selected_model: Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) with Safety Stock — (r, Q) continuous-review policy
research_insights.selection_rationale: EOQ model selected because demand is smooth (CV=16.87%) and continuous — high daily volumes with 100% non-zero fraction suit a continuous-review (r,Q) framework. Normal approximation for safety stock is appropriate given the smooth regime. MOQ of 212,171 is dominated by the EOQ of 1,433,992, so the economic quantity governs.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Low — capacity utilisation at 72.3% leaves adequate headroom. The EOQ order quantity plus safety stock (1,588,560 units) is comfortably within the 2,196,381-unit storage limit. No capacity-driven reduction required.
